hypothesis: Variability (coefficient of variation) of human stature and weight tracks the rate of growth, falling as growth slows and rising in adolescence.
pass_criterion: Across single-year age groups, the correlation between sex-specific CV of stature (or weight) and the growth velocity (cm per year) is above 0.5, with a CV rise at the adolescent spurt.
fail_criterion: Correlation below 0.2 or negative, or no CV rise at ages 10-14.
interpretation: Growth rate comes from cross-sectional differences in mean stature by age. Longitudinal velocity would be better, but the survey is cross-sectional.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
dataset.publisher: CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: Examination data include measured standing height and weight by age and sex.
